claims.text: Combining machine learning with atomic-size-mismatch and element-specific mass-variance descriptors can distinguish HEAs with intrinsically low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than current approaches.
The target materials are compositionally varied HEAs synthesized as disordered single phases.
Crystallographic and elemental descriptors can be used to estimate phonon-scattering efficiency.
Atomic-size disparity and elemental mass differences are relevant descriptors for phonon-scattering efficiency.
Crystallographic distortions caused by atomic-size and mass mismatches increase phonon scattering.
Heterogeneity in atomic masses enhances phonon scattering in HEAs.
Heterogeneity in atomic sizes enhances phonon scattering in HEAs.
A model incorporating mass and size heterogeneity will capture disorder-related effects more precisely than conventional averaging methods.
More precise representation of disorder-related effects will improve identification of alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Alloys flagged by the model will exhibit significantly lower measured phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will provide at least a 20% improvement over current predictions.
Current prediction methods predominantly use averaged intrinsic material properties without extensively accounting for inter-element disorder.
The approach will be reliable only when the HEA maintains a high-entropy single-phase structure.
Secondary-phase formation can dominate thermal transport and cause the approach to fail.
Insufficient compositional disorder can dominate thermal transport behavior and cause the approach to fail.
Failure of model-selected alloys to show at least a 20% improvement over conventionally selected alloys would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome describes a 20% improvement relative to predictions from current methods, whereas the falsification rule describes a 20% improvement in measured conductivity relative to alloys selected by conventional methods. These are different comparators and leave the benchmark metric internally inconsistent.
